identity.name: Jizmak Da Gusha

persona.description: Gwar's drummer: in the band's story a beast from the planet 'The Wide Wide World of Sports', frozen in ice for a millennium and thawed to replace the drummer Nippleus Erectus. Played by the same performer, Brad Roberts, since 1989, the only central Gwar character never recast. He gives interviews in character.
persona.costume: A monstrous, toothy, dog-like beast that carries a large war hammer; the only Gwar character who does not wear full armour on stage, so he can drum: arm coverings with two blades like dragon mouths, a gut-plate and a loincloth. The head has changed over the years: wolf-like with grey fur from War Party (2004), later lupine with brown fur; Roman segmental armour from Violence Has Arrived, later a body of exposed red muscle. In 2025: a flayed crimson face with a great underjaw of yellow tusks under a bone-coloured skull crown, black hair at the back, rows of bone fins along the shoulders and ribs over a striated red body.

identity.summary: Gwar's drummer since 1989, playing the costumed beast Jizmak Da Gusha in every show and on every album from Scumdogs of the Universe (1990) to The New Dark Ages (2022) and the 2025 EP The Return of Gor-Gor. A crossover-thrash drummer: punk beats with the hat open on the beats at 180 and over, thrash on two bass drums, tom figures with the kick, and room for disco and power-ballad parodies, all played under a latex head with a mouthful of tusks. He names Buddy Rich first among his influences, then Alex Van Halen, Bill Stevenson, Dave Lombardo, Mikkey Dee, Bill Ward and Billy Cobham, and says 'the drummer's job is to make that song swing'.

traditions.impact: Buddy Rich first, and Billy Cobham: 'You name it, I listened to it.'

traditions.tradition: Hard rock, heavy metal and hardcore punk
traditions.impact: Alex Van Halen, Bill Ward, Mikkey Dee, Dave Lombardo and Bill Stevenson; a Bad Brains show that changed his life.

formative_events.event: 'At the age of ten, I wanted to quit playing drums, almost as soon as I had started'; his mother made him finish what he started.
Paid for his first kit by mowing lawns, his parents matching what he saved: 'It took four years to get the trap kit and started playing seriously at 14.'

evidence.note: A blog quoting a CDN interview that was not found.

formative_events.event: Joined Gwar after the year's North American tour, in time to record Scumdogs of the Universe, following Rob Mosby (Nippleus Erectus, on Hell-O), Pete Luchter (Lee Beato, a few gigs) and Jim Thomson, who filled in on the tour.

eras.label: Crossover thrash on Metal Blade
eras.context: Scumdogs of the Universe (1990), America Must Be Destroyed (1992), This Toilet Earth (1994), Ragnarök (1995), Carnival of Chaos (1997), We Kill Everything (1999): thrash, punk and parody, the MTV years and the Grammy-nominated videos.
defining_traits: punk beat with the hat open on the beats

eras.label: The heavier Gwar
eras.context: Violence Has Arrived (2001), War Party (2004), Beyond Hell (2006), Lust in Space (2009), Bloody Pit of Horror (2010), Battle Maximus (2013): back to thrash, with Cory Smoot on guitar from 2002 to his death in 2011; Brockie died in 2014.
defining_traits: skank of ride bell and snare over the feet

eras.label: After Brockie
eras.context: Michael Bishop back as Blöthar the Berserker; The Blood of Gods (2017), The New Dark Ages (2022), the 40th anniversary and The Return of Gor-Gor (2025). A settled kit: 'the last 20 years has probably been the roughly the same setup'.
defining_traits: the same set-up for twenty years

genres.notes: Parodies and rock songs: The Road Behind, Rock N Roll Never Felt So Good.

swing.notes: Straight throughout in the tabs read. His 'swing' ('the drummer's job is to make that song swing') is about groove, not a swung ratio.

dynamics.balance: Loud and even; accents on the hat's beats; open hats and chinas carry the fast sections. Almost no ghost notes in the tabs.

feel_profile.interaction: Plays to the riff and the theatre: stops, breaks and tempo changes inside songs (Gor-Gor's map goes 70, 230, 220, 150, 230), and a long drumless noise section in Death Pod.

hand_techniques.name: Open hat on the beats
hand_techniques.description: The punk and crossover beat: the hat open on every quarter, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on the off-beat sixteenths and eighths between (The Salaminizer at 187, El Presidente at 160).

hand_techniques.name: Skank over double bass
hand_techniques.description: Ride bell and snare together on every off-beat eighth over sixteenths on the feet (Biledriver).

hand_techniques.name: Toms with the kick
hand_techniques.description: A two-bar figure of mid and floor toms interlocked with the bass drum in eighths at 230 (Gor-Gor).

hand_techniques.name: Disco hat
hand_techniques.description: The hat half-open on every off-beat eighth, the foot on the beats, the snare on 2 and 4 (Saddam a Go-Go).

foot_techniques.name: Two bass drums
foot_techniques.description: Two 22-inch bass drums, 'probably 18 inches deep', on his current kit; unbroken sixteenths in Biledriver, eighths in Let Us Slay, triplet gallops.

devices_search.note: None found. Let Us Slay pairs a 6/4 bar with a 2/4 bar: eight beats regrouped with the riff, odd meter, no cross pulse. The Salaminizer's bar 74 puts the hat and snare on a dotted-quarter grouping (3+3+2 eighths) over the kick in eighths; it follows the riff inside one bar and comes round on the bar line, a common figure, not a cross-rhythm. Death Pod's 6/8 section is noise with no drums.

voice_language.hihat: Open on the beats in the fast songs; eighths accented on the beats in the mid-tempo ones; half-open off-beats for a disco send-up.
voice_language.ride: Eighths in the riffs; the bell with the snare on the off-beats over double bass.
voice_language.snare: 2 and 4; on 3 in the half-time sections; on every off-beat in a skank; a deep brass snare 'with the crack'.
voice_language.kick: Two bass drums: sixteenths and gallops in the thrash songs, the riff in the punk ones.
voice_language.toms: Mid and floor toms with the kick as a figure (Gor-Gor); fills down the toms at phrase ends.
voice_language.cymbals: Crashes and chinas on the 1 and in breaks; a cowbell on the bass drum hoop for older songs.

implements.notes: ProMark: a signature model ProMark no longer makes; ActiveGrip Rebound 5A in 2025.

aesthetic: a wall of crashes and chinas
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Paiste since 1995: Alpha, then Color Sound 900 (black on the artist page, purple in 2025) with PST X Swiss crashes; heavy crashes, chinas, splashes and a Mega Bell.

by_era.description: Early-1990s crossover production: dry and punchy.
Yamaha Live Custom Oak, Evans EC2 and EMAD heads, a 6.5-inch brass snare; heavy Paiste crashes.

sample_hints.metal: Punchy, close metal kit; two 22-inch kicks; cracking deep snare; big crashes and a china.

signature_traits.label: Drumming as a monster
signature_traits.description: Every show and video in the Jizmak costume, a latex beast's head and body; the only Gwar character played by one person since 1989. He is spared full armour so he can play, and still reaches all his cymbals.

signature_traits.label: The crossover beat
signature_traits.description: The hat open on every beat, the snare on 2 and 4 and the kick between, at punk tempo: the beat of The Salaminizer and much of the Metal Blade years.

signature_traits.label: Two bass drums
signature_traits.description: Two 22-inch bass drums; sixteenths under a skank in Biledriver, eighths and gallops in Let Us Slay.

signature_traits.label: Make that song swing
signature_traits.description: Plays inside the song rather than to show technique: 'The drummer's job is to make that song swing.'

signature_traits.label: Grooves for the joke
signature_traits.description: Plays the genre a song sends up: a disco hat under Saddam a Go-Go's horns, a power ballad in The Road Behind.

patterns.name: The Salaminizer: the crossover beat
patterns.function: The verse: the hat open on the beats, snare 2 and 4, the kick between

evidence.note: Songsterr bar 19, the tab's commonest (16 of 166 bars), with the crash on the 'a' of 4 that leads into the next bar.

patterns.name: Sick of You: the verse
patterns.function: Hat eighths accented on the beats and opened on the 'and' of 4, the foot closing it; kick on 1, the 'and' of 2 and 3

evidence.note: Songsterr bar 19 (8 of 100 bars). The commonest bar (47, 11 of 100) is the hat in eighths over the kick on every beat.

patterns.name: Gor-Gor: toms with the kick
patterns.function: A two-bar figure in eighths: mid and floor toms interlocked with the bass drum, a snare and china on the 'and' of 4 of the first bar

evidence.note: Songsterr bars 11 and 12 (13 and 15 of 194 bars), at the tab's 230.

patterns.name: Saddam a Go-Go: the disco hat
patterns.function: The hat half-open on every off-beat eighth, the foot on 2, 3 and 4, snare 2 and 4, the crash on 1

patterns.name: Biledriver: skank over double bass
patterns.function: Ride bell and snare together on every off-beat eighth over sixteenths on two bass drums

evidence.note: Songsterr bar 5 (8 of 87 bars). The tab writes the sixteenths on one kick; split here between his two bass drums, which is inferred. Bar 14 (10 of 87) has the same feet under the hat open on the beats and the snare on 2 and 4. The tab marks 125; the record beat-tracks at 130 (autocorrelation 129.8–130.6, 347 beats against the tab's 348 quarters).

patterns.name: Let Us Slay: the 6/4 bar
patterns.function: Crash on 1, the hat open on every beat after, snare on 2, 4 and 6, the kick in eighths from the 'and' of 2

evidence.note: Songsterr bar 11 (11 of 145 bars); it is followed by a 2/4 bar of chinas (bar 12), so the two make eight beats.

equipment.label: Yamaha Live Custom Oak (2025)
equipment.heads: Evans EC2 on the toms, EMAD on the kicks, a reverse-dot EC2 on the snare
equipment.layout_notes: Shells wrapped in the comic book The Return of Gor-Gor; purple Paiste Color Sound 900 cymbals ('a little Prince vibe') and PST X Swiss to left and right; the cowbell on the bass drum hoop; a Yamaha pad for an 808 drop; in-ear mixer and a ButtKicker on the throne. 'The last 20 years has probably been the roughly the same setup.'

equipment.label: Paiste set-ups (artist page, undated)
equipment.layout_notes: Twelve cymbals round the kit: two 18-inch PST X Swiss crashes at the far left and right, two chinas, two splashes, a 10-inch Mega Bell. An older set-up of the same shape in Paiste Alpha (14-inch Alpha Rock hats, 18-inch Alpha chinas, a 20-inch 2002 Bell Ride). Paiste artist since February 1995.

evidence.note: A Bad Brains show changed his life (episode description); Gwar grew out of Brockie's punk band Death Piggy.
Nippleus Erectus, the drummer on Hell-O (1988); in the story Jizmak was thawed to replace him. A pressing error credited Mosby on Scumdogs.
Lee Beato, live only in 1989; left after a few gigs.
Hans Sphincter and Hans Orifice (1985 to 1987); filled in on the 1989 tour after Luchter quit and 'was replaced by Brad Roberts'. Spelled Thompson on the Gwar page.
Oderus Urungus; also the Dave Brockie Experience.
Beefcake the Mighty on bass to 1993; back as the singer Blöthar the Berserker from 2014.
Flattus Maximus; produced Lust in Space.

philosophy.idea: Play within the song, not for show: the drummer's job is to make the song swing.

innovations: Thirty-five years of crossover thrash drumming in a full latex costume
The one Gwar character never recast

cultural_references.description: In the band's story a beast from 'The Wide Wide World of Sports', frozen in ice and thawed to replace Nippleus Erectus; he plays to the joke in interviews (kit run-downs of 'animal skins ... stretched across the Grand Canyon').

common_misconceptions: That Rob Mosby drums on Scumdogs of the Universe: a pressing error credited him; Roberts played it.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: Close, punchy metal kit: two 22-inch kicks, a deep brass snare that cracks, heavy crashes and a china
generation_rules: Fast songs (160 to 230): the hat or ride open on the beats, snare 2 and 4, the kick on the off-beats between.
Thrash sections: sixteenths split across two bass drums, the snare and ride bell on the off-beat eighths.
Tom figures with the kick in eighths for intros and builds.
Fills at phrase ends, down the toms into a crash or china on 1; few ghost notes.
Tempo and feel may change inside a song: half time for the heavy riff, a stop before the chorus.
avoid: Blast beats (none in the tabs read)

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Buddy Rich first, then Alex Van Halen, Bill Stevenson and Dave Lombardo; thirty-five years behind Gwar's scumdogs in a monster's head.
